clue.text: Daydreaming, having an inclination 'to take a holiday?

parts.note: someone on holiday is away from work, that is absent
minded means disposed or inclined to do something

explanation.surface: A dreamy worker who fancies some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the two halves in reverse order: the inclination (MINDED) is named first but comes second in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in a daydream is forgetful and inattentive, which is the sense of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Making a note to prepare a speech

parts.note: D is one of the notes of the musical scale
to dress is to prepare, as when a cook dresses a chicken or a salad

explanation.surface: Someone jots down a reminder before writing a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech delivered to an audience is called an address.

clue.text: Move stiffly — support required

explanation.surface: Walking awkwardly because a brace is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk in a stiff, swaggering way is one sense; the other is a bar or brace that props up a structure.

clue.text: Getting involved in action over a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the A that follows it
involved suggests tangled together, so the letters of the words in and action are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone joins in a fight after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting involved' mixes IN and ACTION into NICOTIAN; 'over' puts that above A in this down answer. 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotiana is the tobacco plant, grown in gardens for its scented flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: It preserved an old soldier's letters

explanation.surface: An old veteran kept his wartime correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads as a soldier keeping letters, but means the chain armour that kept a medieval soldier alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain armour protected knights of old; separately, the post brings letters and parcels.

clue.text: A number of bonds for a person's latter years?

parts.note: nine is a number
ties are bonds that join things together

explanation.surface: An investor's portfolio of bonds put aside for old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonds' suggests finance and pensions, but here it simply means ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged ninety to ninety-nine is in their nineties, the decade near the end of a long life.

clue.text: Aim to get around the foreign beast

indicators.note: get around tells us the word for aim encircles the other piece

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
la is the French for the

explanation.surface: A hunter aims to stalk an exotic animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an animal or beast.

clue.text: Transport for those with a one-track mind

definitions.text: Transport for those with a one-track mind

parts.words: Transport for those with a one-track mind
parts.note: a joke on an obsessive person, read literally as a railway running on a single track

explanation.surface: A vehicle for single-minded obsessives.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway running on one rail is a form of transport using a single track.

clue.text: Used a comb and so caused irritation

explanation.surface: Someone fussed with their hair and annoyed people.
explanation.definitionFit: Backcombing hair to make it bushy is one sense; the other is mocking or provoking someone.

clue.text: Bearing an order

explanation.surface: Carrying an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearing is a compass heading or course, and an instruction from a conductor or director is another sense.

clue.text: Originated from highest grade blossom

parts.note: A is the top mark or grade in an exam
a rose is a blossom

explanation.surface: A prize flower came from top stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To have come into being or sprung from something is the meaning of this past tense verb.

clue.text: . English country property

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A stately home in the English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large landed property with a house and grounds is called an estate.

clue.text: Academic boss wanting acknowledgements. of indebtedness

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament
IOUs are written notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A university head is short of credit notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager, but it means a stud, a knob on a surface. The stray full stop is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish person who devotes time to study is academic in temperament.

clue.text: Savoury paste for a feast

explanation.surface: Pâté laid out for a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A paste put on bread is one sense; a lavish meal laid out on a table is the other.

clue.text: A game permitted in the road

indicators.note: in tells us the word for permitted sits inside the word for road

parts.note: a route is a road or way
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Children allowed to play in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling pastime with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Sinister and abandoned hired man

parts.note: left means deserted or abandoned
a hand is a hired labourer, as in a farmhand

explanation.surface: A sinister farmworker left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' looks like menacing, but in heraldry it means on the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is the Latin and heraldic word for the left side.

clue.text: A speculator — perhaps he tries to acquire gold

indicators.note: to acquire means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
perhaps signals the letters of the words he tries may be set out differently

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A prospector keeps trying to find gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals the anagram of HE TRIES (giving THEISER), and 'to acquire' puts the heraldic gold inside it. 'Speculator' suggests finance, but here it means a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms speculative theories is a speculator in ideas, not money.

clue.text: Putting a stop to publicity

explanation.surface: Halting an advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping up a hole is one sense; giving something repeated promotion is the other.

clue.text: Meritorious religious leader at one time very competent

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1630s
able means skilled or competent

explanation.surface: Praise for a capable cleric of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUD was an Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I, head of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserving praise is worthy or meritorious.

clue.text: Gave tongue, though subdued

explanation.surface: Someone spoke out though beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass the tongue over something is one sense; to defeat or beat is the other.

clue.text: A neat hanger

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is something that hangs from an ox or cow

explanation.surface: A tidy coat-hanger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of loose skin under a cow's throat hangs down from its neck.

clue.text: A. Greek god in the main not immutable

definitions.text: A. Greek god in the main not immutable

parts.words: A. Greek god in the main not immutable
parts.note: a sea deity of Greek myth famous for changing his shape at will

explanation.surface: A Greek sea deity who keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the sea. The stray full stop is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This old man of the sea in Greek myth could take any form, so he was changeable.

clue.text: Prison in which curtailed liberty causes deep division

indicators.note: in which means the next piece goes inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a prison

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: leave is liberty, permission to be absent

explanation.surface: Restricted freedom in jail creates a rift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberty' is leave in the military sense of permitted absence; 'curtailed' drops its final E (giving LEAV), and 'in which' puts that inside the prison word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split or sharp divide between groups or parties.

clue.text: A composer's drive to compose

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads a composer is

indicators.note: to compose means to arrange, so the letters of drive are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A composer's urge to write music.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian who wrote Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: With all speed find some cash. :Balance nil!

parts.note: P is a penny, a small amount of cash
the rest is the balance or remainder
O looks like zero, nil

explanation.surface: Hurry and find money, as the bank balance is zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction for very fast, used generally for quickly.

clue.text: Disdain to urge a point

parts.note: to spur is to urge on
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Refusing to press a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject with contempt is to disdain.

clue.text: A boom? Dispute that

explanation.surface: Someone queries an economic upturn.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a ship's pole, a spar; to argue or box is the other sense.

clue.text: Chemical compound used in pesticides — terribly harmful

indicators.note: used in shows the answer is found inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A dangerous chemical in crop sprays.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Deception of a naughty child sure to go wrong

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: go wrong signals that the letters of sure to are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mischievous child tells a lie that misfires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go wrong' is the anagram signal for SURE TO (giving OSTURE); 'naughty' with 'child' points to the mischievous sprite of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending to be someone else is a fraud or deception.

clue.text: Handy means of identification .

parts.note: handy here means from the hand, so the marks left by the hand that police use to identify people

explanation.surface: A convenient way to prove who you are.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridged marks left by the tips of the digits are unique to each person.
